properties.description: Whether to disable this EIP from the route during build time. Once an EIP has been disabled then it cannot be enabled later at runtime.

properties.name: correlationExpression
properties.description: The expression used to calculate the correlation key to use for aggregation. Exchanges with the same correlation key are aggregated together. If the correlation key cannot be evaluated an Exception is thrown.

properties.name: completionPredicate
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: A predicate to indicate when an aggregated exchange is complete. If not specified and the AggregationStrategy implements Predicate, it will be used as the completionPredicate.

properties.name: completionTimeoutExpression
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Time in millis that an aggregated exchange should be inactive before its complete (timeout), evaluated as an expression allowing dynamic timeout values.

properties.name: completionSizeExpression
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Number of messages aggregated before the aggregation is complete, evaluated as an expression allowing dynamic size values.

properties.name: optimisticLockRetryPolicy
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Configures retry settings when using optimistic locking.

properties.name: parallelProcessing
properties.description: When completed exchanges are sent out of the aggregator, this option indicates whether Camel should use a thread pool with multiple threads for concurrency.

properties.name: optimisticLocking
properties.description: Turns on optimistic locking, which requires the aggregation repository to implement OptimisticLockingAggregationRepository.

properties.name: optimisticLockingSyncRetry
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: When optimistic locking is enabled, retries happen synchronously in the same thread instead of being scheduled on a background thread. This preserves transaction context for repositories that require single-thread transactional guarantees.

properties.name: executorService
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Reference to a custom thread pool to use for parallel processing and sending out aggregated exchanges.

properties.name: timeoutCheckerExecutorService
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Reference to a custom thread pool for the background completion timeout checker.

properties.name: aggregateController
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Reference to an AggregateController to allow external sources to control this aggregator.

properties.name: aggregationRepository
properties.description: Reference to the AggregationRepository to use. By default uses MemoryAggregationRepository.

properties.name: aggregationStrategy
properties.description: The AggregationStrategy to use. Required. Merges each incoming exchange with the existing already merged exchanges. At first call the oldExchange parameter is null.

properties.name: aggregationStrategyMethodName
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: The method name to use when using a POJO as the AggregationStrategy.

properties.name: aggregationStrategyMethodAllowNull
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: If true then null is used as the oldExchange at the very first aggregation, when using POJOs as the AggregationStrategy.

properties.name: completionSize
properties.description: Number of messages aggregated before the aggregation is complete. Can also be set as an expression via completionSizeExpression.

properties.name: completionInterval
properties.description: A repeating period by which the aggregator will complete all current aggregated exchanges. Cannot be used together with completionTimeout.

properties.name: completionTimeout
properties.description: Time that an aggregated exchange should be inactive before its complete (timeout). Cannot be used together with completionInterval.

properties.name: completionTimeoutCheckerInterval
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Interval in millis for the background task that checks for completion timeouts. Default is 1000 (1 second).

properties.name: completionFromBatchConsumer
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Enables batch completion mode where aggregation completes based on the total number of exchanges reported by a batch consumer. Cannot be used together with discardOnAggregationFailure.

properties.name: completionOnNewCorrelationGroup
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Enables completion on all previous groups when a new incoming correlation group starts. Only one correlation group can be in progress at a time.

properties.name: eagerCheckCompletion
properties.description: If enabled then the completion predicate evaluates against the incoming exchange. Otherwise it evaluates against the aggregated exchange.

properties.name: ignoreInvalidCorrelationKeys
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: If enabled then a correlation key that cannot be evaluated is logged and ignored, instead of throwing an exception.

properties.name: closeCorrelationKeyOnCompletion
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Closes a correlation key when its complete. Late arriving exchanges with a closed correlation key will throw a ClosedCorrelationKeyException. The value is the maximum cache size of closed keys. Use 0 for unbounded.

properties.name: discardOnCompletionTimeout
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: If enabled then the aggregated message is discarded (dropped) on completion timeout instead of being sent out of the aggregator.

properties.name: discardOnAggregationFailure
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: If enabled then the partly aggregated message is discarded when aggregation failed (an exception was thrown from AggregationStrategy). Cannot be used together with completionFromBatchConsumer.

properties.name: forceCompletionOnStop
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: If enabled then all current aggregated exchanges are completed when the context is stopped.

properties.name: completeAllOnStop
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: If enabled then waits to complete all current and partial (pending) aggregated exchanges when the context is stopped, ensuring the aggregation repository is empty before shutdown.

properties.description: Configures the size of the sliding window which is used to record the outcome of calls when the CircuitBreaker is closed. Sliding window can either be count-based or time-based.

properties.name: slidingWindowType
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Configures the type of the sliding window which is used to record the outcome of calls when the CircuitBreaker is closed. Sliding window can either be count-based or time-based.

properties.name: slidingWindowSynchronizationStrategy
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Configures the synchronization strategy for the sliding window. LOCK_FREE uses a CAS-based lock-free algorithm for better performance under high concurrency. SYNCHRONIZED uses blocking locks with lower memory allocation.

properties.name: minimumNumberOfCalls
properties.description: Configures the minimum number of calls which are required (per sliding window period) before the CircuitBreaker can calculate the error rate.

properties.name: writableStackTraceEnabled
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Enables writable stack traces. When set to false, Exception.getStackTrace returns a zero length array. This may be used to reduce log spam when the circuit breaker is open.

properties.name: waitDurationInOpenState
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Configures the wait duration which specifies how long the CircuitBreaker should stay open, before it switches to half open. The default is 60 seconds.

properties.name: automaticTransitionFromOpenToHalfOpenEnabled
properties.displayName: Automatic Transition From Open To Half Open Enabled
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Enables automatic transition from OPEN to HALF_OPEN state once the waitDurationInOpenState has passed.

properties.name: maxWaitDurationInHalfOpenState
properties.displayName: Max Wait Duration In Half Open State
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Configures the maximum wait duration which controls how long the CircuitBreaker should stay in Half Open state, before it switches to open. Value 0 means circuit breaker will wait in half open state until all permitted calls have been completed.

properties.name: slowCallRateThreshold
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Configures a threshold in percentage. The CircuitBreaker considers a call as slow when the call duration is greater than slowCallDurationThreshold. When the percentage of slow calls is equal or greater the threshold, the CircuitBreaker transitions to open and starts short-circuiting calls.

properties.name: slowCallDurationThreshold
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Configures the duration threshold above which calls are considered as slow and increase the slow calls percentage. The default is 60 seconds.

properties.description: Whether bulkhead is enabled or not on the circuit breaker.

properties.name: bulkheadMaxConcurrentCalls
properties.description: Configures the max amount of concurrent calls the bulkhead will support.

properties.name: bulkheadMaxWaitDuration
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Configures a maximum amount of time which the calling thread will wait to enter the bulkhead. The default is 0 (no waiting).

properties.name: bulkheadFairCallHandlingEnabled
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Configures whether the bulkhead uses a fair calling strategy. When enabled (default), a fair strategy guarantees the order of incoming requests (FIFO). When disabled, no ordering is guaranteed and may improve throughput.

properties.name: asynchronous

When enabled, the circuit breaker releases the caller thread immediately and completes processing asynchronously. This is most valuable when the downstream processor supports asynchronous processing (e.g. Netty HTTP, Kafka). When used with timeout, the timeoutExecutorService must be a ScheduledExecutorService.

properties.name: timeoutExecutorService

properties.description: References to a custom thread pool to use when timeout is enabled (uses ForkJoinPool.commonPool() by default).

properties.name: timeoutDuration

properties.name: timeoutCancelRunningFuture

properties.name: micrometerEnabled

properties.name: parallelAggregate
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: If enabled then the aggregate method on AggregationStrategy can be called concurrently. Notice that this would require the implementation of AggregationStrategy to be implemented as thread-safe. By default this is false meaning that Camel synchronizes the call to the aggregate method. Though in some use-cases this can be used to archive higher performance when the AggregationStrategy is implemented as thread-safe.

properties.name: parallelProcessing
properties.description: If enabled then processing each split message occurs concurrently. The caller thread still waits until all messages are fully processed before it continues.

properties.name: synchronous
properties.description: When enabled then the same thread is used to continue routing after the split is complete, even if parallel processing is enabled.

properties.name: streaming
properties.description: When enabled then the splitter splits the original message on-demand, and each split message is processed one by one. This reduces memory usage as the splitter does not split all messages first.

properties.name: stopOnException
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: If enabled then stops further split processing if an exception or failure occurred during processing of a split message, and the caused exception will be thrown. The default behavior is to not stop but continue processing till the end.

properties.name: timeout
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Total timeout in millis when using parallel processing. If the splitter has not been able to process all replies within the given timeframe, then the timeout triggers and the splitter breaks out and continues.

properties.name: executorService
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Reference to a custom thread pool to use for parallel processing. Setting this option implies parallel processing.

properties.name: onPrepare
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Reference to a processor for preparing the exchange to be sent. Can be used to deep-clone messages that should be sent.

properties.name: shareUnitOfWork
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Shares the unit of work with the parent and each of the split messages. By default each split exchange has its own individual unit of work.

properties.name: group
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Groups N split messages into a single message with a java.util.List body. This allows processing items in chunks instead of one at a time.

properties.name: errorThreshold
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Sets the error threshold as a fraction (0.0-1.0) of failed items before aborting the split operation. For example, 0.1 means abort if more than 10% of items fail. When the threshold is exceeded, a org.apache.camel.CamelExchangeException is thrown. This option is mutually exclusive with stopOnException . When set, individual item failures are tracked but processing continues until the threshold is exceeded. Note: When combined with parallelProcessing , the failure ratio may vary between runs because parallel items complete in non-deterministic order. For deterministic abort behavior with parallel processing, prefer maxFailedRecords (absolute count) over errorThreshold (ratio).

properties.name: maxFailedRecords
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Sets the maximum number of failed records before aborting the split operation. When the count is exceeded, a org.apache.camel.CamelExchangeException is thrown. This option is mutually exclusive with stopOnException . Can be combined with errorThreshold processing aborts when either threshold is exceeded.
